packet.headline_seed: Food delivery rider wins China's top literary prize

what: Food delivery rider wins China's top literary prize

clean_source_blocks.text: Wang Jibing is among blue-collar Chinese workers gaining wider attention for their literary works.

Wang Jibing, a food delivery rider, posted his poems and essays on social media for years before going viral A collection of poems, some scribbled on slips of paper between food deliveries, has won Wang Jibing one of China's top literary honours. Low Flight, inspired by the everyday challenges delivery riders face, has bagged the Lu Xun Literary Prize - named after a writer who has been referred to as the father of modern Chinese literature. Wang, 56, who became a delivery rider around 2019, gained traction on social media for his poems and essays. He is part of a growing group of blue-collar workers who are being celebrated for their literary works, which offer a glimpse into the pressures that they face in China's massive gig economy.

Food delivery rider and poet Wang Jibing has won one of China’s highest literary honors, the Lu Xun Literary Prize, for his poetry collection “Low Flight.” The prize, announced July 15 and in its ninth edition, honored 35 works across seven categories. The award was established in 1996 in memory of the renowned Chinese writer Lu Xun and is given every four years. Wang, a 57-year-old from the eastern Jiangsu province, is known as “a delivery rider by day and a poet by night.” Since becoming a food delivery rider in 2019 in the province’s Kunshan city, he has logged over 150,000 kilometers on the road and written more than 6,000 poems inspired by his deliveries and life.

by Xinhua writers Yu Xiaohua and Wang Xiaopeng BEIJING, July 15 (Xinhua) -- He is a man racing against time. Somehow, he has learned to catch it on paper. Wang Jibing, a 56-year-old delivery rider, has earned one of China's most prestigious literary honors with verses born in the fleeting moments spent waiting for meals to be delivered, elevators and customers. His poetry collection, "Di Chu Fei Xing," which translates as "Low Flight," was announced one of the winners of the ninth edition of Lu Xun Literature Prize on Wednesday. This collection captures the unvarnished realities and emotional subtleties of his life as one of the country's more than 10 million food delivery riders.

Low Flight, inspired by the everyday challenges delivery riders face, has bagged the Lu Xun Literary Prize - named after a writer who has been referred to as the father of modern Chinese literature.

Wang, 56, who became a delivery rider around 2019, gained traction on social media for his poems and essays.

He is part of a growing group of blue-collar workers who are being celebrated for their literary works, which offer a glimpse into the pressures that they face in China's massive gig economy.

For Wang, the prestigious literary prize comes after a few difficult decades as an odd job worker.

"I held my breath and felt extremely nervous… Once it was revealed, everything was settled,"  Wang told state media outlet Global Times on 15 July, when news broke that he had won the award - adding that the media attention around him had created a lot of mental pressure on him.

But his love for reading persisted, and over the last decade he has been posting his own poems and essays on social media.

In 2022, one of his poems, titled Man in a Hurry, went viral online. It was inspired by a incident in 2019, in which he spent hours on a frustrating delivery after a customer entered the wrong address.

In 2023 he published his first poetry collection, Man in a Hurry: Poems of a Food Delivery Rider.

Food delivery rider and poet Wang Jibing has won one of China’s highest literary honors, the Lu Xun Literary Prize, for his poetry collection “Low Flight.”

The prize, announced July 15 and in its ninth edition, honored 35 works across seven categories. The award was established in 1996 in memory of the renowned Chinese writer Lu Xun and is given every four years.

Wang, a 57-year-old from the eastern Jiangsu province, is known as “a delivery rider by day and a poet by night.” Since becoming a food delivery rider in 2019 in the province’s Kunshan city, he has logged over 150,000 kilometers on the road and written more than 6,000 poems inspired by his deliveries and life.

In recent years, grassroots writers like Wang have gained increasing recognition in China. They include former miner Chen Nianxi, whose poetry and nonfiction stories document the lives of Chinese workers; Yu Xiuhua, a former farmer whose candid poems dissect subjects such as love, desire, and living with cerebral palsy; and Hu Anyan, a former courier whose book, “I Deliver Parcels in Beijing,” details the strain of gig-economy work.

Another outlet is the Picun Literature Group, a collective of migrant worker writers based in an urban village on the outskirts of Beijing. In 2017, group member Fan Yusu’s autobiography, “I Am Fan Yusu,” became a nationwide hit.

“I made deliveries yesterday, and as long as I live in Kunshan, I’ll keep delivering food,” Wang said after receiving the award. He has previously said that food delivery had since become his “side hustle,” alongside literary events and book royalties.

“Low Flight” is Wang’s third published collection. For it, he interviewed more than 140 delivery riders in hopes that readers “would better understand the challenges they face.”

payload.title: Ruokalähetti Wang Jibing sai yhden Kiinan merkittävimmistä kirjallisuuspalkinnoista
payload.summary: Wang Jibing palkittiin lähetintyön arkea kuvaavasta runokokoelmastaan. Sixth Tone kertoo hänen kirjoittaneen yli 6 000 runoa.
payload.content:
Ruokalähettinä työskentelevä Wang Jibing on saanut yhden Kiinan arvostetuimmista kirjallisuustunnustuksista runokokoelmastaan Di Chu Fei Xing, jonka nimi voidaan kääntää muotoon Matala lento. Lu Xun -kirjallisuuspalkinnon yhdeksännen kierroksen voittajat julkistettiin 15. heinäkuuta. Wangin kokoelma perustuu hänen kokemuksiinsa ruokalähettinä ja kuvaa työn kiirettä, odotuksia sekä arjen tunnevivahteita.

## Tuhansia runoja toimitusmatkoilta

[Sixth Tone](https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018783) kertoo Wangin aloittaneen ruokalähettinä vuonna 2019 Kunshanin kaupungissa Itä-Kiinan Jiangsun maakunnassa. Julkaisun mukaan hän on sen jälkeen kulkenut työssään yli 150 000 kilometriä ja kirjoittanut yli 6 000 runoa. Niiden aiheet ovat syntyneet toimitusmatkoilla, asiakkaiden luona ja muissa lähetintyön hetkissä, joissa aikataulu määrää päivän tahdin. Sixth Tone kuvaa Wangia ruokalähetiksi päivisin ja runoilijaksi öisin.

Kaikki tekstit eivät ole syntyneet rauhallisessa työtilassa. Wang on kirjoittanut säkeitä pienille paperilapuille odottaessaan ravintoloissa annoksia, rakennuksissa hissejä tai ovilla asiakkaita. Hän julkaisi runojaan ja esseitään sosiaalisessa mediassa vuosien ajan ennen kuin ne levisivät laajalle ja toivat hänelle enemmän lukijoita. Sosiaalisen median kautta toimitusten lomassa syntyneet kirjoitukset tavoittivat vähitellen aiempaa suuremman yleisön.

## Kokoelma kuvaa alustatalouden arkea

Kiinan valtiollinen [Xinhua-uutistoimisto](http://www.chinaview.cn/20260715/c5b1f7279e1e484196aeb709fb613a02/c.html) kertoo, että Di Chu Fei Xing kuvaa Wangin työn kaunistelematonta arkea ja hienovaraisia tunteita. Wang on yksi maan yli kymmenestä miljoonasta ruokalähetistä. Kokoelman taustalla ovat lyhyet pysähdykset, jatkuva liike ja työ, jossa aikaa vastaan kilpaillaan. Palkinto nostaa samalla esiin Wangin kaltaisia ruumiillisen työn tekijöitä, joiden kirjallisuus avaa näkymän Kiinan laajan alustatalouden paineisiin.

Sixth Tone kertoo myös, että Lu Xun -kirjallisuuspalkinto perustettiin vuonna 1996 tunnetun kirjailijan Lu Xunin muistoksi ja jaetaan neljän vuoden välein. Julkaisun mukaan palkinnon yhdeksännellä kierroksella tunnustuksen sai yhteensä 35 teosta seitsemässä kategoriassa. Wangin runokokoelma oli yksi näistä teoksista, ja tunnustus kuuluu Kiinan merkittävimpiin kirjallisuuspalkintoihin.

Wangin kokoelman syntytapa osoittaa, että lähetin ja runoilijan roolit lomittuvat myös kesken työpäivän. Hän on tarttunut hetkiin, jolloin ruokalähetti joutuu odottamaan ruokaa, hissiä tai asiakasta, ja muuttanut havaintonsa runoiksi. Palkinto tuo nämä työn sisältä kirjoitetut kokemukset entistä laajemman yleisön nähtäville.

Sixth Tone kertoo myös, että Lu Xun -kirjallisuuspalkinto perustettiin vuonna 1996 tunnetun kirjailijan Lu Xunin muistoksi ja jaetaan neljän vuoden välein. Julkaisun mukaan palkinnon yhdeksännellä kierroksella tunnustuksen sai yhteensä 35 teosta seitsemässä kategoriassa. Wangin runokokoelma oli yksi näistä teoksista, ja tunnustus kuuluu Kiinan merkittävimpiin kirjallisuuspalkintoihin.

Wangin kokoelman syntytapa osoittaa, että lähetin ja runoilijan roolit lomittuvat myös kesken työpäivän. Hän on tarttunut hetkiin, jolloin ruokalähetti joutuu odottamaan ruokaa, hissiä tai asiakasta, ja muuttanut havaintonsa runoiksi. Palkinto tuo nämä työn sisältä kirjoitetut kokemukset entistä laajemman yleisön nähtäville.

article.source_text:
Wang Jibing is among blue-collar Chinese workers gaining wider attention for their literary works.

Wang Jibing, a food delivery rider, posted his poems and essays on social media for years before going viral A collection of poems, some scribbled on slips of paper between food deliveries, has won Wang Jibing one of China's top literary honours. Low Flight, inspired by the everyday challenges delivery riders face, has bagged the Lu Xun Literary Prize - named after a writer who has been referred to as the father of modern Chinese literature. Wang, 56, who became a delivery rider around 2019, gained traction on social media for his poems and essays. He is part of a growing group of blue-collar workers who are being celebrated for their literary works, which offer a glimpse into the pressures that they face in China's massive gig economy.

Food delivery rider and poet Wang Jibing has won one of China’s highest literary honors, the Lu Xun Literary Prize, for his poetry collection “Low Flight.” The prize, announced July 15 and in its ninth edition, honored 35 works across seven categories. The award was established in 1996 in memory of the renowned Chinese writer Lu Xun and is given every four years. Wang, a 57-year-old from the eastern Jiangsu province, is known as “a delivery rider by day and a poet by night.” Since becoming a food delivery rider in 2019 in the province’s Kunshan city, he has logged over 150,000 kilometers on the road and written more than 6,000 poems inspired by his deliveries and life.

by Xinhua writers Yu Xiaohua and Wang Xiaopeng BEIJING, July 15 (Xinhua) -- He is a man racing against time. Somehow, he has learned to catch it on paper. Wang Jibing, a 56-year-old delivery rider, has earned one of China's most prestigious literary honors with verses born in the fleeting moments spent waiting for meals to be delivered, elevators and customers. His poetry collection, "Di Chu Fei Xing," which translates as "Low Flight," was announced one of the winners of the ninth edition of Lu Xun Literature Prize on Wednesday. This collection captures the unvarnished realities and emotional subtleties of his life as one of the country's more than 10 million food delivery riders.
